APCTT-C01.quote: Because several directly measured parameters are strongly correlated with particular constituents of interest, regression models provide a valuable tool for evaluating variability and loading on the basis of computed continuous data.
APCTT-C01.note: Basis: surrogate relations between sensor measurements and constituents; OLS regression with cited methods (p16).

APCTT-C02.quote: In addition, the information can be used to assess water qual-ity relative to TMDLs, NPDES requirements, water-quality standards, BMPs, and stream management goals.
APCTT-C02.note: Application and use of the monitoring and estimation system.

APCTT-C03.quote: Water-quality conditions are quantified among the watersheds of similar size (50.1 square miles to 65.7 square miles) using continuous, in-stream mea-surements, and using regression models developed from con-tinuous and discrete data.
APCTT-C03.note: Computed concentrations and loads show the system's key function.

APCTT-C04.note: Borderline: discrete samples were analysed in laboratories with replicate QA (p16), but the monitoring system itself was not tested in a laboratory.

APCTT-C05.quote: Each monitor was located within the stream cross-sec-tion to be representative of conditions across the width of the stream, which was verified using cross-section measurements during different streamflow and seasonal conditions (Rasmus-sen and others, 2008).
APCTT-C05.note: Monitors verified in the streams; regression models developed from site samples with 90-percent prediction intervals (p16).

APCTT-C06.quote: Streamflow-gaging stations and continuous water-quality monitors (fig. 2) were installed at five stream sites in John-son County, Kansas (fig. 1, table 1).
APCTT-C06.note: System deployed at the five sites.

APCTT-C07.quote: These data are available in real-time on USGS Web pages (http://nrtwq.usgs.gov/ks/ and http://waterdata.usgs.gov/ks/nwis/current/?type=qw).
APCTT-C07.note: Operating in the actual environment with real-time public delivery.

APCTT-C08.note: Borderline: maintenance and reporting followed standard USGS procedures (p14), but no qualification of the final system against requirements.

APCTT-C09.quote: Monitors operated from January 2003 through December 2007 in Cedar Creek (USGS station 06892495), from January 2003 through December 2008 in Mill Creek (station 06892513), from January 2004 through December 2007 in Kill Creek (station 06892360), and from January 2004 through December 2011 in the Blue River (station 06893100) and Indian Creek (station 06893390).
APCTT-C09.note: Operation over stated multi-year periods at named sites.

APCTT-C10.note: The many criterion comparisons (dissolved oxygen, chloride, turbidity, E. coli) concern stream water quality, not the system's performance against its requirements.

APCTT-C11.quote: Monitor maintenance and data reporting followed standard procedures described in Wagner and others (2006).
APCTT-C11.note: Monitor placement, operating periods, sample collection (18-28 samples per site, p16) and models described.

APCTT-C12.quote: The U.S. Geological Survey, in cooperation with the Johnson County Stormwater Management Program, began a comprehensive study of John-son County streams in 2002 to evaluate and monitor changes in stream quality.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the Johnson County monitoring and regression-estimation system.

notes: Organizer estimate TRL 7. C09 is met on the checklist (multi-year operation at stated sites) but C08 is not shown, so this labeller's opinion is TRL 8, low confidence.
